title: Secrets Guard Operator: upgrade, observability and rollback sketch
content:
Purpose
This note captures a lightweight playbook for upgrading the Secrets Guard Operator (SGO) used in private deployments, plus companion Terraform module guidance and observability hardening. Audience: infra engineers preparing on-prem / VPC customers for an SGO operator upgrade that affects KMS/HSM bindings, secret mirroring, and audit delivery.

Goals and scope
- Perform a safe, reversible upgrade of the SGO and related Terraform modules with minimal customer downtime.
- Ensure KMS/HSM integrations remain deterministic (no key lineage breakage).
- Improve audit log fidelity and introduce sampling for high-volume customers.
- Deliver Terraform changes in an idempotent manner and provide rollback paths for both operator and infra.
- Provide a testing matrix and short-circuit checklist for last-minute go/no-go decisions.

Non-goals
- This doc does not replace formal runbooks for key-ceremony. It assumes customer has valid HSM procedures and attestation tokens in place.

High-level approach
1) Dual-write compatibility window: ensure the new SGO can write wrapped secrets to both existing KMS backend and the new HSM adapter for a configurable transition period.
2) Observability-first rollout: enable verbose auditing and request sampling at canary scope before full rollout.
3) Terraform module staged apply: split infra changes into two commits: a read-only validation apply (plan + drift detect) and then an apply with guarded state changes.
4) Automated acceptance tests: preflight test suite that validates unwrap/reencrypt round-trip using test keys only.

Pre-upgrade checklist (must pass before canary)
- All active customers using SGO identified (list exported).
- Backup state: snapshot Terraform state, store in long-term bucket with retention tag.
- Key audit: verify active KMS keys and HSM slots, ensure key metadata (key_version_id, creation_time, labels) exported.
- Attestation tokens present for HSM nodes and not expiring during the window.
- Monitoring baseline captured (7d metrics): per-token latency, KV cache hit ratio, secrets write errors.
- Canary namespace prepared: isolated VPC or test-tenant with the same KMS/HSM profile.

Terraform module notes (implementation hints)
- Module layout: split into 3 modules: redwood_sgo_core, redwood_kms_bindings, redwood_hsm_adapter. Keep state for each module separate (backend config) to reduce blast radius.
- Version pinning: use semver for modules (v2.7.x) and pin provider versions in root to avoid drift.
- Idempotency: ensure resources that mutate secrets are marked with lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["data"] } where appropriate to prevent accidental overwrite on plan/apply.
- Plan-only validation: create a CI job that runs terraform plan against customer state (read-only credentials) and stores the plan artifact with a checksum.
- Migration helpers: provide a terraform data source redwood_sgo_migration that returns a migration plan (list of secrets to dual-write) for the apply step.
- Drift detection: use periodic terraform plan schedules and alert on any diff in redwood_kms_bindings.

KMS/HSM compatibility and key lineage
- Avoid re-encrypting ciphertext blobs unless key metadata requires it; prefer wrapping metadata updates with a forwarding pointer (metadata.v1 -> metadata.v2) to maintain provenance.
- For HSM-backed keys: maintain a mapping table (hsm_slot_id -> key_alias) in state, and do not reassign slots during the rolling upgrade.
- Key rotation policy: perform rotation in two phases: 1) stage new key in HSM and ensure operator can use it, 2) reprovision secrets using the new key with a TTL-based cutover.

Secrets mirroring and atomic rotation pattern
- Dual-write model: SGO writes to both KMS and HSM backends with a monotonic migration id. Readers prefer HSM ciphertext when migration_id >= M.
- Read-path fallback: when HSM unwrap fails, fall back to KMS unwrap and emit an audit record with error_code=UNWRAP_HSM_FAIL.
- Atomic toggle: expose a feature-flag in operator config (migration.window.enabled) to move traffic at tenant granularity.

Observability and audit log design
- Audit schema: timestamp, tenant_id, secret_id (hashed), operation, src_backend, dst_backend, result_code, latency_ms, operator_version, actor_id. Keep secret values out of logs.
- High-volume sampling: for tenants with >2500 ops/min, sample 1% of reads and 100% of writes. Label sampled events with sample_rate=0.01.
- Trace context: propagate trace_id through unwrap/re-encrypt calls and correlate with serving traces.
- Alert rules: generate alerts for unwrap error rate > 0.5% sustained over 10m, and for any HSM slot error.
- Long-tail debugging: add a debug toggle that creates a temporary, time-limited copy of the failed ciphertext into a secure bucket for post-mortem.

Canary plan and acceptance tests
- Canary scope: 3 tenants (low, med, high throughput) in isolated env.
- Test cases: 
  * unwrap existing KMS-wrapped secret with new SGO -> expect success, compare plaintext digest.
  * dual-write secret creation -> both backends should return valid ciphertexts.
  * simulate HSM node restart -> operator should fallback to KMS and resume.
  * audit delivery test -> verify events in audit ELT within 30s.
- Performance gate: per-token latency regression < 5% p50, p95 thresholds preserved.
- Security gate: no plaintext logs, all audit events redact secret values.

Rollback strategy
- Operator rollback: revert operator image to the previous tagged release and set migration.window.enabled=false. Operator will then prefer KMS ciphertexts again.
- Terraform rollback: apply the exported state snapshot. If state drift prevents simple revert, run targeted resource replaces for redwood_hsm_adapter resources with the prior resource ids.
- Emergency key unwrap: provide an offline tool (sgo-unwrap-cli) that given privileged creds can attempt to unwrap using previous KMS key material in a maintenance window.
- Communication: pre-baked incident Slack channel and customer notification templates in templates/upgrade-failure/ (linked in artifacts).

Post-upgrade hardening (next 30 days)
- Reduce verbose audit logging to baseline and keep critical ops at 100% retention.
- Run a forensic scan for any unexpected fallback unwraps.
- Schedule a full key-ceremony review for HSM keys used in the migration.

Open questions / risks
- HSM vendor behavior for slot reallocation under firmware upgrades is vendor-specific; need vendor-specific test harnesses.
- Some customers may have constrained attestation renewal windows; coordinate before scheduling.
- Terraform state split reduces blast radius but increases operational complexity for cross-module changes.

Implementation TODOs (short term)
- Add migration.data_source to terraform module (owner: Priya) - JIRA-4819.
- Add audit sampling flag to operator config + observability dashboard (owner: Marta) - JIRA-4824.
- Build sgo-dual-write acceptance suite in CI and run nightly against a synthetic canary (owner: Liam) - JIRA-4832.
- Draft customer-facing upgrade checklist and email template (owner: Evan) - draft in linked artifacts.

Appendix: quick terraform snippet (illustrative only)
resource "redwood_kms_key" "sgo_migration_key" {
  name = "sgo-migration-${var.tenant_id}"
  purpose = "ENCRYPT_DEK"
  rotation_period_days = 90
}

module "sgo_core" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//sgo_core?ref=v2.7.3"
  tenant_id = var.tenant_id
  kms_key = redwood_kms_key.sgo_migration_key.id
  enable_migration_window = var.enable_migration_window
}

Notes: do a terraform plan output to a file and verify the migration list before applying. Keep manual approvals on any resource replacement.

-- end of sketch --
